CVE-2026-123012.description: In Gogs 0.14.3, the Git Smart HTTP authorization layer in internal/route/repo/http.go allows a push when only read access was intended, a different vulnerability than CVE-2026-52810. This occurs because of a case-sensitivity desync between the authorization classifier and the request dispatcher: the gitHTTPIsPull function compares the Git action verb case-sensitively and defaults to pull (read access) for any unrecognized string, whereas the request dispatcher lowercases the same verb before routing it to the receive-pack handler. Capitalizing a single letter in the URL (e.g. info/Refs instead of info/refs, or git-receive-Pack instead of git-receive-pack) causes the classifier to misidentify a push as a pull, granting only read-level authorization, whereas the dispatcher routes it to the write handler. An authenticated read-only collaborator can exploit this to push to a private repository, creating, updating, or deleting refs.

CVE-2026-129304.title: Guard Core: Unvalidated X-Forwarded-For-derived string used as a Redis key component and interpolated into a KEYS glob pattern
CVE-2026-129304.description: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, _extract_from_forwarded_header() in guard_core/utils.py returns the selected X-Forwarded-For entry without validating that it is an IP address. In deployments configured with trusted_proxies where the selected entry is attacker-controlled, the arbitrary client_ip string reaches BehaviorTracker in guard_core/handlers/behavior_handler.py and is interpolated into Redis key names and blocking KEYS glob patterns. Glob metacharacters can cause one request to count other clients' behavior events, embedded separators can disturb key parsing, and rotating identities can create unbounded keys while repeatedly scanning the shared Redis keyspace. A non-IP identity can also reach a ban action and cause an uncaught validation error. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

CVE-2026-134791.title: Unclosed Comments Make the Lexer of ExpressionLanguage Quadratic, Letting Untrusted Expressions Hold a Process
CVE-2026-134791.description:
Since Symfony 7.2, expressions can contain comments. The lexer used a regular expression to find the end of a comment. When a /* was never closed, this regular expression scanned the rest of the expression, and the lexer then went on with the next character. So each /* scanned the rest of the expression again. Linting 192 KB of /* took 9 to 11 seconds, and 96 KB took 34 seconds without PCRE JIT.

The lexer runs before the parser and its nesting limit. Any code that lints or parses untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. A Length constraint on the same value doesn't help, since the validator runs both constraints.

The lexer now uses strpos() to find the end of a comment, and a comment that is never closed throws a SyntaxError. Such expressions were already invalid. Lexing takes linear time again.
